verdicts.strongest_argument: The load-bearing novelty premise is factually FALSE, and I can quote the refutation twice. The claim says Q4 FY2025 revenue is 'a figure the company has never reported and that only exists as FY2025 US$118.0m minus nine-month FY2025 US$87,390,942.' The company reported it verbatim on 2025-09-09, in a PR Newswire release furnished on EDGAR as ex99-1 to 6-K 0001493152-25-012895, under section headers 'Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Highlights' and 'Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2025 Unaudited Financial Results': 'Total revenue was US$30.7 million, representing a 2.9% decrease from US$31.6 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024.' Gamehaus reports every standalone quarter with a call and a transcript; nothing here requires cross-document subtraction. On top of that, the US$23-26m Q4 guide is published guidance given 2026-06-08 and carried by PR Newswire, TradingView, Manila Times, StockTitan, Benzinga, Globe and Mail, thestockobserver, scanx and grafa. Both operands of the YoY division are in wire copy; the division is one keystroke. Separately, the derived base is slightly wrong: using the reported 30.7 the range is -15.3% to -25.1%, not -15.0% to -24.8%. And the magnitude read is one-sided: the company printed at or above the TOP of its guide in Q2 (26.3 vs 24-27) and Q3 (26.2 vs 24-26), so a 26.0 print gives -15%, i.e. 1.6x the prior decline rate, not 3x; meanwhile net income rose YoY for three straight quarters (+17.6%, +151.2%, +16.4%) on a 10.1% opex cut, which is the framing the wires actually used ('Q3 revenue exceeds guidance as margins expand'). The one genuinely unwritten piece is that the guide breaks Q4 seasonality (Q4 FY2025 was +6.6% sequential; the guide implies -12% to -1%). That is worth something, but not much on a name where the guide itself is a month old and public.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every quoted word is verbatim from a PR Newswire release dated 2026-08-12 and is therefore in the wire copy 27 days before the print. It was syndicated to AOL and headlined by StockTitan as 'Gamehaus Shifts Strategy to AI Content Tools.' The claim's own tape evidence also cuts against it in a way the claim does not report: yes, only 22,908 shares traded on 2026-08-12 and the stock went $0.79 to $0.74 to $0.70 (-11.4%, and I confirm those closes exactly) — but on 2026-08-14 it printed +7.66% to $0.76 on 142,571 shares, six times the release-day volume, so two-thirds of the markdown was reversed within one session on higher volume. The market saw it, marked it down, and un-marked it. The residual edge is genuinely there and is why this is not an 80: the release quantifies nothing, and the Sep 8 call will attach a Q1 FY2027 revenue guide to a deliberate wind-down of the revenue base — and social casino is unambiguously the base (three of the five apps in GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD's Apple account are Bingo Island, Vegas Party Casino Slots and Double Win Slots; the top Google Play titles are Double Rich Casino Slots and Lucky Hit Classic Casino Slots). A first quantification of a self-inflicted revenue decline is new. The strategy statement is not.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a claim about the price rather than about the company, so almost by construction it is in the price. Every element is either on EDGAR or on the public tape: I confirm 2026-08-31 close $0.85, +16.51%, volume 7,314,944 (stockanalysis.com), and I confirm the 6-K of 2026-08-28 states the program was extended to 2027-08-28 with 'approximately 518,063 Class A Ordinary Shares for approximately US$600,000' repurchased. I also confirm the 5-day run-up is arithmetically that one session: 2026-08-28 $0.73 to 2026-09-04 $0.82. And the fade is already visible without waiting for the print — $0.85, $0.84, $0.82, $0.79, $0.82 across 08-31 to 09-04, i.e. the market gave back a quarter of the spike in three sessions on its own. The precedent is also published: the original US$5m authorisation was press-released on 2025-08-28 and Investing.com reported the stock 'soars', with the surge widely put at ~93%. The one thing the claim adds that is not written anywhere is the reading that a 6-K-only extension of a program 12% used is not information — but that reading is a baseline correction, not an edge, and the correction is one the tape has already begun making.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The promise half is fully published and I verified it verbatim in three places (Globe and Mail, Benzinga transcript, thestockobserver, all 2026-06-08): one RPG in commercial testing for end-Q2-calendar-2026 in Hong Kong/Macau/Taiwan, a second custom-developed RPG 'on track for launch around September', a third signed for an August-to-September window, and 'the user base to return to growth as multiple new titles launch through fiscal 2027'. The absence half is not published anywhere and I confirm the observation as far as it goes: GAMEHAUS PTE. LTD's Apple developer page lists exactly five apps — North Tower! Merge TD Defense, Match Tile Scenery, Bingo Island, Vegas Party Casino Slots, Double Win Slots — and not one is an RPG. But the negative evidence is methodologically weak in three ways the claim does not address. Gamehaus is a publisher of third-party titles, so an RPG 'signed for global distribution' plausibly ships under the developer's own Apple account. The first RPG was explicitly to launch 'initially in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan', which are separate App Store storefronts that a US-storefront developer page does not enumerate. And Apple developer pages do not reliably surface soft-launched or region-limited titles. So this is absence of evidence in the one place where evidence would least be expected. Worse for its independence: the reason the Aug 12 release does not mention the RPG pipeline is that the Aug 12 release announces a different strategy — which is GMHS#1. The two claims are one fact seen from two sides.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component is on EDGAR, and I verified each one verbatim. The Class B increase from fifteen to fifty votes was approved 2026-07-10 and reported in the 6-K filed 2026-07-14 (27,765,163 for, 20,686 against at the Class A meeting), and it is then restated in the F-3 prospectus itself: 'each Class B Ordinary Share carries fifty (50) votes'. The F-3 of 2026-07-28 registers 'up to US$200,000,000' and states on its cover 'US$23,523,531.54 based on the closing price of US$0.87 per Class A Ordinary Share on July 27, 2026 and 27,038,542 Class A Ordinary Shares held by non-affiliates' — the claim's figures are exact. The F-3 itself discloses the I.B.5 baby-shelf constraint and that no securities were sold under it in the prior twelve months, so the ~US$7.8m unused capacity is disclosed by the company, not discovered. StockTitan indexed the EFFECT notice on 2026-08-12 for retail. What is left is the 'sequence' framing, and the entrenchment leg of it is economically null: with 15,598,113 Class B at fifteen votes against 37,971,245 Class A (FY2025 20-F), insiders already controlled ~86% of the vote. Going to ~95% moves nobody from minority to control; it changes nothing about who decides anything, and it transfers no value on its own. The dilution leg is real — US$7.8m against a ~US$45-53m cap is ~15-17% potential dilution and is large against US$18.3m of cash — but it is capacity, not a deal, and it does not resolve on Sep 8. A raise after the print is a scenario, not this print.

One unresolved discrepancy worth flagging: the 2026-07-14 6-K's general-meeting tally (136,978,599 for, described as ~82.3% of total voting power) implies total voting power of ~166.5m, which cannot be reconciled with 15,598,113 Class B at fifteen votes plus ~49.5m Class A (~283m). verdicts.strongest_argument: I verified this precisely, including the specific document: Yan Xi's Form 3, event date 2026-03-18, reports 5,314,953 Class A ordinary shares held indirectly through Joystick Holding Limited, with Director / 10% Owner / Chief Technology Officer boxes checked. Six Form 3s were filed 2026-03-18 and a seventh on 2026-04-03, and the company did subsequently file 6-Ks and, on 2026-07-28, a Form F-3 — a form only a foreign private issuer may use. So the anomaly is real. It is also worth exactly nothing to this print. A Form 3 is an initial statement: it reports no transaction, no purchase, no sale and no change in holdings, only that a pre-existing insider now has a filing obligation. There is no cash flow, no dilution and no disclosure content in it. And the natural bearish reading — that Gamehaus lost foreign private issuer status and must convert to 10-K/10-Q — does not survive the dates: FPI status is tested on the last business day of the second fiscal quarter, 2025-12-31 for a June year end, and a failure there takes effect on the first day of the next fiscal year, 2026-07-01, not 2026-03-18; and the F-3 filed 2026-07-28 is direct evidence the company still considers itself an FPI. The most parsimonious explanation is a counsel-side filing error or a prophylactic filing, which is a governance-hygiene datum with no valuation content and no path to Sep 8. Nothing in the Q4 release will confirm or deny it.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I ran the search myself and the factual core is correct: EDGAR full-text search for 'Third Quarter of Fiscal 2026' under CIK 0002000530 returns zero hits, 'Fiscal 2026' returns only the 2025-11-25 and 2026-03-23 6-Ks, the complete 6-K list has nothing on or near 2026-06-08 or 2026-08-12, and the last EDGAR-visible revenue datapoint is indeed the US$26.3m December 2025 quarter in the 2026-03-23 exhibit. That is a genuine, unwritten observation and it is why this is not an 80. But the inference it carries — that the market therefore cannot see the numbers — is refuted by the record. The 2026-06-08 Q3 release is on PR Newswire, TradingView, Manila Times, StockTitan, Globe and Mail, thestockobserver, scanx and grafa, and Benzinga published the full call transcript. The 2026-08-12 release is on PR Newswire, AOL and StockTitan. Anyone with a newsfeed has both. Nor is the omission clearly irregular: Rule 13a-16 requires an FPI to furnish information it makes public under home-country law, files with an exchange, or distributes to security holders, and many FPIs do not 6-K interim press releases; Nasdaq's public-disclosure obligation is satisfied by PR Newswire. So the premise that this is a compliance lapse is itself contestable. Most importantly, this claim is a transmission mechanism, not a driver: it is the reason GMHS#0 and GMHS#1 might be under-absorbed, and it has no independent effect on the Sep 8 price. Nothing in it resolves at the print.

interactions: Heavy overlap; at most three of the seven are independent. (1) GMHS#1 and GMHS#3 are one fact from two sides: the 2026-06-08 RPG-led growth story was superseded nine weeks later by the 2026-08-12 AI-content story, which is why the Aug 12 release omits the RPG pipeline. Counting the strategy change and the missing RPG trace as two negatives double-counts the same event. (2) GMHS#0 and GMHS#3 rest on the same document, the 2026-06-08 Q3 release and call. (3) GMHS#6 is explicitly a transmission mechanism for GMHS#0 and GMHS#1 rather than a driver — it has size_check 0.0 on its own and its entire value is conditional on the other two being real; and its premise is largely refuted by the same wire trail that GMHS#0 and GMHS#1 cite as sources, so it partly undercuts them. (4) GMHS#0's stated novelty mechanism is refuted by a document sitting under the very CIK that GMHS#6 full-text searched: the 2025-09-09 6-K exhibit reports Q4 FY2025 revenue as US$30.7m twice, verbatim, so no cross-document subtraction was ever needed. (5) GMHS#1 and GMHS#4 compete for the same price move: the F-3 EFFECT notice and the AI-strategy release both landed 2026-08-11/12, so the -5.99% on 2026-08-12 cannot be attributed to either alone, and each claim is quietly relying on it. (6) GMHS#2 and GMHS#4 point the same way and neither says so: an unused, effective US$7.8m baby shelf plus a one-day 16.5% spike on 27% of the non-affiliate float is precisely the setup for an opportunistic raise into strength. That is the most coherent bear mechanism in the brief and no claim states it. (7) Notable absence: none of the seven mentions the 6-K of 2026-07-13 disclosing a Nasdaq minimum-bid-price deficiency with a 2027-01-06 compliance deadline. That is arguably the largest published overhang on the name, it gives GMHS#2's buyback extension an obvious motive, and it materially changes how a sub-$1 quote should be read.
